subject: Cloud Computing
title: Private Endpoints and Service Mesh
description: A quick, practical guide to Private Endpoints and Service Mesh.

hook.text: Your app talks to a cloud database. By default, that traffic might cross the public internet. That's a risk.

buildup.text: Private endpoints keep traffic between your services inside the cloud provider's private network.

discovery.text: AWS PrivateLink and Azure Private Endpoints create secure, private connections to cloud services.

twist.text: A service mesh adds another layer: it encrypts and controls all traffic between your own microservices.

climax.text: Private endpoints and service mesh together mean no sensitive traffic ever touches the public internet.

punchline.text: Keep internal traffic internal. The public internet is not your friend.

quiz.question: What do private endpoints do?
options: Keep traffic between services inside the cloud's private network
Make cloud services accessible from the public internet
Encrypt user passwords stored in databases

details.summary: Private endpoints let cloud services communicate over private network paths instead of the public internet, while service meshes manage encrypted communication between microservices automatically. Together they eliminate unnecessary exposure of internal traffic.
details.whyItMatters: Internal service-to-service traffic is an attractive target for lateral movement. Private endpoints and service meshes reduce the network attack surface without requiring application changes.
takeaways: Private endpoints keep service traffic off the public internet
Service meshes automate mTLS between microservices
Both reduce lateral movement opportunities for attackers

faq.question: What is a service mesh?
faq.answer: A service mesh is an infrastructure layer that manages communication between microservices using sidecar proxies. It handles encryption, load balancing, retries, and observability without modifying application code. Istio and Linkerd are popular implementations.

faq.question: Do private endpoints eliminate the need for encryption?
faq.answer: No. Private endpoints reduce exposure but traffic still crosses shared provider infrastructure. Defense in depth demands encrypting data in transit even on private networks. Combine private endpoints with TLS for comprehensive protection.
